findings.issue_text: Authorization logic uses && instead of || for isTeamAdminOrOwner, denying plain team admins
Blacklisted guest emails bypassed via case variation since blacklist is lowercased but guest email compared raw
Case-insensitivity miss in attendee dedupe check allows duplicate attendee rows via case variants
Server trusts client-side uniqueness; schema and handler never dedupe guests, causing duplicate attendees and emails via direct API calls
Booking state never checked; guests can be added to cancelled/completed bookings triggering calendar updates and emails for dead events
Email failure silently swallowed with console.log and success response returned to user
sendAddGuestsEmails called with raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, causing wrong template selection for pre-existing attendees
Organizer lookup crashes for bookings with userId null, throwing raw Prisma error as unhandled 500
EventManager built from ctx.user instead of booking.user, so calendar update may use credentials without access to organizer's calendar
isInvalidEmail validation error state never cleared on success/reopen, showing stale warning in dialog
Error toast renders 'undefined: ...' when err.data is absent; t(err.message) renders raw keys; message fallback is dead code
MultiEmail list keyed by index with splice removal causes stale/uncontrolled input state when removing middle rows
Broken authorization: permission check grants access to any attendee (isAttendee), allowing attendees to add arbitrary guests to bookings they were invited to (P0, IDOR-style missing ownership check)
Attendee-added guests trigger sendAddGuestsEmails to all attendees + organizer + team members spoofed from the organizer's address, enabling email bombing/spam relay
Added guests receive an ICS REQUEST with full event details including video call URL/password, letting attendees grant third parties access to private meeting links
No cap on guests.length and no rate limiting on the addGuests mutation
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of || so a user must be both admin and owner of the team to pass, denying legitimate team admins
Blacklist check bypassable via case/whitespace mismatch: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but guests compared raw, so 'Attacker@x.com' or ' guest@x.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
Dedupe vs existing attendees uses exact match, so case/whitespace variants create duplicate attendees for the same person
guests array has no max() in the Zod schema, allowing authorized callers to add thousands of attendees in one mutation
Calendar update uses the calling user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so the update fails or writes to the wrong calendar when an attendee or non-owner team admin triggers the mutation
Seat-limited bookings bypass capacity: handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot but never validates booking.attendees.length + uniqueGuests.length <= seatsPerTimeSlot
booking.userId null causes findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) to throw, surfacing as an unhandled 500 for bookings with no assigned user
Attendee identity check uses exact non-normalized email match (attendee.email === user.email), so case differences can cause legitimate organizers/co-attendees to fail the isAttendee check
Unbounded guest list input: guests array has no .max() cap, enabling massive fan-out of DB writes, synchronous email fan-out, and spam/abuse vector
Coarse cache invalidation: utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() refetches all bookings queries instead of only the affected booking
Duplicate-attendee growth: case-sensitive email dedup comparison creates duplicate attendee rows for emails differing only in case
Synchronous email sending in mutation path: await sendAddGuestsEmails serially renders N email payloads, multiplying latency with attendee count; should be backgrounded/queued
Redundant per-attendee translation fetches: getTranslation awaited per attendee though locales are shared; could be memoized per unique locale
Authorization logic inverted: `&&` requires BOTH admin AND owner instead of either, so team admins get FORBIDDEN on bookings they should manage (addGuests.handler.ts ~48)
`teamId ?? 0` for non-team bookings makes both isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner checks fail, relying incidentally on isOrganizer to cover it
Calendar update uses the caller's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the organizer's, so attendee-triggered addGuests fails silently or updates the wrong calendar
Server schema does not enforce guest email uniqueness; duplicate emails pass validation and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows (addGuests.schema.ts:5)
Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but guest is compared raw, so 'Guest@spam.com' bypasses the blacklist
Attendee dedupe `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, allowing an already-attending guest to be re-added
Client schema doesn't trim emails, causing inconsistent email validation behavior between UI and API (zod .email() trimming varies by version)

Organizer email subject uses calEvent.attendees[0].name instead of team?.name || organizer.name, naming the wrong party and drifting from all other organizer email templates (organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26)
Subject template accesses attendees[0].name which throws if the attendees array is empty
prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws a raw Prisma P2025 surfaced as opaque 500 instead of a typed TRPCError when booking.userId is null
No seat-capacity validation: seatsPerTimeSlot is read but current attendee count is never checked against capacity before createMany, allowing guests beyond capacity for seated event types
Handler returns ad-hoc non-localized raw string { message: "Guests added" } instead of structured data, making untranslated server text part of the public mutation contract
P1: Authorization logic uses && instead of || in addGuests.handler.ts:55-58, so team admins must also be team owners to pass, causing FORBIDDEN errors for legitimate admins
P2: Server accepts duplicate guests within a single request in addGuests.handler.ts:66-72; dedupe only checks existing attendees, allowing direct tRPC calls to create duplicate attendee rows
P2: Blacklist check is case-inconsistent (addGuests.handler.ts:60-72); guest emails are compared raw against lowercased blacklist entries, allowing bypass via different casing

P2: Calendar update failure at addGuests.handler.ts:160-161 is outside try/catch and runs after the Prisma write, leaving DB mutated with no rollback and no emails sent; retry dead-ends on uniqueness check
P2: Email send errors silently swallowed in addGuests.handler.ts:163-167; error object discarded, wrong console.log used, and user gets success toast even if zero emails delivered
P2: No cap on number of guests per request (addGuests.schema.ts:3-5); array has no max(), enabling mass attendee creation and email fan-out as a spam/DoS vector
P3: Client error toast fallback is dead code (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-46); message is always non-empty so t('unable_to_add_guests') unreachable, and t(err.message) may render raw keys
P3: isInvalidEmail flag never cleared on retry (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:55-63); stale warning remains visible even after user fixes emails and the request succeeds

Broken authorization logic in addGuests.handler.ts: uses `&&` instead of `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so users must be both admin and owner to pass; team admins or owners alone are denied and the admin/owner branch is effectively dead logic

Effective authorization degrades to 'organizer or any existing attendee', allowing any attendee to add arbitrary guests to a booking and trigger emails/calendar updates (potential unintended privilege escalation)
Stale pre-update `booking` object is passed to eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees instead of the updated `bookingAttendees`, so new guests may never be synced to the calendar

Case-sensitive duplicate/blacklist filtering: `guest === attendee.email` and blacklistedGuestEmails comparison don't lowercase the guest, so `User@example.com` bypasses the blacklist and creates duplicate attendees

Client-side zod schema in AddGuestsDialog duplicates ZAddGuestsInputSchema; uniqueness rule exists only on the client, so the server doesn't enforce it — reuse the shared server schema and move uniqueness validation server-side
Error message reuse: `emails_must_be_unique_valid` is used for the 'all guests already exist' case instead of a proper error message

Swallowed error in catch block logs a static string ('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') instead of the actual error, making email failures undebuggable; should log err with bookingId via the repo's logger

BookingListItem renders the add_members action for every booking without checking booking.status, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/rejected bookings; should gate the action and/or validate status server-side
Validation error state `isInvalidEmail` is never reset on email edits or dialog reopen, only on cancel, so the error sticks for the dialog's lifetime
onError uses `t(err.message)` assuming the message is always a translation key; non-TRPC errors render raw text and `${err.data?.code}` leaks internal error codes into the UI toast
MultiEmail uses array index as React key in value.map, which can cause stale input state on removal/reordering; prefer a stable id per row
P1: Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so team admins (non-owners) are wrongly forbidden at addGuests.handler.ts:60-66
P1: Any booking attendee can add an unbounded list of guests with no cap or per-booking status check, enabling email bombing via ICS REQUEST emails even on cancelled/rejected bookings
P1: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees will no-op or fail when a non-organizer triggers the mutation

P1: Partial failure — DB write (prisma.booking.update creating attendees) is committed before updateCalendarAttendees, which is outside the try/catch; a throw leaves guests persisted, emails unsent, and calendar out of sync with no reconciliation

P1: Seated events bypass seat capacity — guests are inserted directly into booking.attendees with no check against seatsPerTimeSlot or the seated-booking seat structure, allowing arbitrary overbooking

P2: Blacklist and attendee dedupe are bypassed by case variation — blacklist emails are lowercased but `guest` is not, and attendee comparison is case-sensitive, allowing blacklisted emails and duplicate attendee rows with duplicate ICS emails
P2: booking.userId can be null (unassigned bookings), causing findFirstOrThrow({id: booking.userId || 0}) to throw a raw Prisma error resulting in a 500 instead of a handled TRPCError

P2: Client-side AddGuestsDialog — multiEmailValue can be non-empty while containing only empty strings so handleAdd silently no-ops with no feedback, and isInvalidEmail is never reset on subsequent attempts, leaving a stale error banner
P2: Server schema only validates z.array(z.string().email()) without a uniqueness check, so direct API calls can submit duplicate guests, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails
P3: Email send errors are swallowed — console.log with no error object and success returned, so nobody learns guests weren't notified

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic uses && instead of || for isTeamAdminOrOwner, denying plain team admins
Blacklisted guest emails bypassed via case variation since blacklist is lowercased but guest email compared raw
Case-insensitivity miss in attendee dedupe check allows duplicate attendee rows via case variants

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe/blacklist logic compares emails case-sensitively: `guest === attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing `guest`/`attendee.email` (while the blacklist is lowercased). This allows adding duplicates via case variants (e.g., `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com`) and can create duplicate attendee rows via `attendees.createMany`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server trusts client-side uniqueness; schema and handler never dedupe guests, causing duplicate attendees and emails via direct API calls
Booking state never checked; guests can be added to cancelled/completed bookings triggering calendar updates and emails for dead events

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched by `id` only (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and then always proceeds to update attendees (`prisma.booking.update`), update calendar attendees (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`), and send emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) with no check for any booking lifecycle/state (e.g., cancelled/completed). If such states exist (common for bookings), this endpoint would still mutate and notify for events that should be inactive, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failure silently swallowed with console.log and success response returned to user

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues to `return { message: "Guests added" }`. This means email delivery failures are not surfaced to the caller and no error details are logged, while the UI will treat the operation as successful.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails called with raw guests instead of uniqueGuests, causing wrong template selection for pre-existing attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` (filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted ones) and only persists those (`createMany` uses `guestsFullDetails` built from `uniqueGuests`). However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original raw `guests` input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, template selection depends on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`: attendees whose email is present in the passed list are treated as “new” and get `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, otherwise they get `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing raw `guests` can incorrectly mark pre-existing attendees (entered again in the dialog) as “new”, causing wrong email template selection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer lookup crashes for bookings with userId null, throwing raw Prisma error as unhandled 500

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`, this coerces to `0`, which will not match a real user and will cause `findFirstOrThrow` to throw (not converted into a `TRPCError`). There is no guard for `booking.userId == null`, so this can crash the mutation for such bookings and surface as a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager built from ctx.user instead of booking.user, so calendar update may use credentials without access to organizer's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller), not the booking organizer (`booking.user`/`booking.userId`). Since the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers (e.g. `isAttendee`), an attendee adding guests will attempt `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using the attendee’s credentials, which likely won’t have access to the organizer’s destination calendar referenced by `booking.destinationCalendar` / `booking.user.destinationCalendar` included earlier in the handler. This mismatch can break calendar attendee updates for non-organizer callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail validation error state never cleared on success/reopen, showing stale warning in dialog

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails (`handleAdd`), but it is not reset in the mutation `onSuccess` handler. Since the dialog component remains mounted (rendered in `BookingListItem` regardless of `isOpenDialog`), reopening the dialog can show the stale warning (`{isInvalidEmail && ...}`) even after a successful add, because only `setMultiEmailValue([""])` and `setIsOpenDialog(false)` are called on success. It is only cleared on the Cancel button path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error toast renders 'undefined: ...' when err.data is absent; t(err.message) renders raw keys; message fallback is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`'s `addGuestsMutation.onError`, the code builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`. If `err.data` (or `err.data.code`) is absent, this will stringify to something like `"undefined: booking_not_found"` (or similar). Then `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never hit the fallback because `message` is always a non-empty string, even when it contains `undefined`. Also `t(err.message)` will often just render the raw key if no translation exists, compounding the poor error output. This behavior is directly implied by the string interpolation in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail list keyed by index with splice removal causes stale/uncontrolled input state when removing middle rows

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list renders inputs with `key={index}` and removes an entry via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. Using array indices as keys in a mutable list can cause React to reuse component instances for different rows after a middle deletion, which can lead to mismatched UI state (e.g., focus/cursor jumping or any internal state inside `EmailField` being associated with the wrong email) even though `value` is passed as a prop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken authorization: permission check grants access to any attendee (isAttendee), allowing attendees to add arbitrary guests to bookings they were invited to (P0, IDOR-style missing ownership check)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the authorization gate explicitly allows any invitee of the booking to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and access is granted unless `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` (i.e., `isAttendee` is sufficient). This means any attendee of a booking can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests` with that `bookingId` and arbitrary `guests` emails (only filtered by existing attendees + `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`), which is an IDOR-style permission issue if attendees are not intended to modify the attendee list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee-added guests trigger sendAddGuestsEmails to all attendees + organizer + team members spoofed from the organizer's address, enabling email bombing/spam relay

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation explicitly allows any existing attendee to add arbitrary guest emails (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...);` and the permission check only forbids when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`). After adding, it always calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which sends emails to the organizer (and team members) plus *every* attendee (`calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`), meaning an attendee can trigger emails to many third-party addresses by submitting a large `guests` list (no rate/size limits shown in the diff). The finding’s “spoofed from organizer” aspect is somewhat overstated, but attendee-driven mass email sending/spam relay is directly enabled by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Added guests receive an ICS REQUEST with full event details including video call URL/password, letting attendees grant third parties access to private meeting links

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation allows any existing attendee to add arbitrary guest emails (`isAttendee` is treated as authorized in `addGuestsHandler`, and only blocks if `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee`). The handler constructs a `CalendarEvent` `evt` that explicitly includes `videoCallData` with `url` and `password` when a video reference exists, then triggers calendar/email updates (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`). In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the newly-added guests (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`) are sent `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, which typically includes an ICS invite; thus an attendee can effectively invite third parties to an event and propagate the private meeting link/password via the calendar/email flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cap on guests.length and no rate limiting on the addGuests mutation

adjudication.rationale: The new addGuests input schema allows an unbounded array (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in `addGuests.schema.ts`) and the handler will `createMany` attendees and send emails based on that list (`addGuests.handler.ts`), so a reviewer can reasonably flag the lack of a maximum size as a potential abuse/perf concern. However, the claim about “no rate limiting” is not fully verifiable from this diff because rate limiting could be enforced in shared TRPC/procedure middleware not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of || so a user must be both admin and owner of the team to pass, denying legitimate team admins
Blacklist check bypassable via case/whitespace mismatch: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but guests compared raw, so 'Attacker@x.com' or ' guest@x.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized with `.toLowerCase()`, but the incoming `guests` values are compared without normalization: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (and also compared to existing attendee emails via `guest === attendee.email`). Since `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only enforces `z.string().email()` and does not lowercase/trim, a mixed-case email like `Attacker@x.com` can bypass a blacklist entry like `attacker@x.com` due to case-sensitive `includes`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dedupe vs existing attendees uses exact match, so case/whitespace variants create duplicate attendees for the same person

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduping uses exact string comparison against existing attendee emails: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist check `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing case (or trimming). Since `addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `z.string().email()` (no normalization) and `AddGuestsDialog` passes user-entered strings directly, case variants like `Test@Example.com` vs `test@example.com` can bypass the check and be inserted via `createMany`, creating duplicates for the same person.

adjudication_records.issue_text: guests array has no max() in the Zod schema, allowing authorized callers to add thousands of attendees in one mutation

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (or other size limit). The handler `addGuestsHandler` then `createMany` attendees and triggers calendar updates plus `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, so an authorized caller could submit a very large `guests` array and cause excessive DB writes, external calendar operations, and email sends in a single mutation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the calling user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so the update fails or writes to the wrong calendar when an attendee or non-owner team admin triggers the mutation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, but the `EventManager` is constructed from the calling session user (`...user`) and credentials fetched with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. If an attendee or other authorized non-organizer triggers `addGuests`, this will use their credentials rather than the booking organizer’s credentials, despite the booking query including `booking.user.credentials` (which then goes unused). This can plausibly fail to update the organizer’s calendar or update the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Seat-limited bookings bypass capacity: handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot but never validates booking.attendees.length + uniqueGuests.length <= seatsPerTimeSlot

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` adds attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any capacity check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`. Although `seatsPerTimeSlot` is read and attached to the `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`), there is no validation like `booking.attendees.length + uniqueGuests.length <= seatsPerTimeSlot`, so seat-limited bookings can exceed capacity by adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: booking.userId null causes findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) to throw, surfacing as an unhandled 500 for bookings with no assigned user

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this becomes `id: 0`, which will typically not exist and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma error. That exception is not caught and would surface as a 500 from the `addGuests` mutation for bookings without an assigned `userId` (the code already anticipates a nullable `userId` by using `|| 0`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee identity check uses exact non-normalized email match (attendee.email === user.email), so case differences can cause legitimate organizers/co-attendees to fail the isAttendee check

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler` authorization logic, attendee status is computed via an exact string comparison: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts). Neither side is normalized (e.g., lowercased/trimmed), so a case difference between the stored attendee email and `user.email` can incorrectly make `isAttendee` false, causing a legitimate attendee to hit the `FORBIDDEN` path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guest list input: guests array has no .max() cap, enabling massive fan-out of DB writes, synchronous email fan-out, and spam/abuse vector

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound, and the UI (`MultiEmail`) lets users append unlimited empty/email fields. In `addGuestsHandler`, the server performs `createMany` DB writes for all `uniqueGuests` and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails`, which fans out emails via `Promise.all` across attendees/team members with no rate/size guard. This enables a single request to trigger large DB work + large synchronous email send volume (spam/abuse/DOS vector) directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Coarse cache invalidation: utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() refetches all bookings queries instead of only the affected booking

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the mutation `onSuccess` calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();`, which (by its name and typical tRPC utils behavior) invalidates the entire `viewer.bookings` query namespace rather than only the specific booking that had guests added. This is a diff-grounded, actionable performance/scope concern (unnecessary refetching) rather than a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate-attendee growth: case-sensitive email dedup comparison creates duplicate attendee rows for emails differing only in case

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication against existing attendees is done with a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist check `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (where blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not). On the client, uniqueness validation uses `new Set(emails)` which is also case-sensitive. Therefore emails differing only by case (e.g., `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com`) will bypass dedup and can be inserted via `createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows for the same underlying address.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous email sending in mutation path: await sendAddGuestsEmails serially renders N email payloads, multiplying latency with attendee count; should be backgrounded/queued

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation awaits `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` inside the request path (`await sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`), which can add noticeable latency proportional to the number of recipients. However, the finding’s claim that emails are sent “serially” is not supported by the diff: `sendAddGuestsEmails` builds an array of promises and uses `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`, indicating concurrent dispatch rather than serial sending. The broader performance/architecture concern (should be backgrounded/queued rather than awaited) is still diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant per-attendee translation fetches: getTranslation awaited per attendee though locales are shared; could be memoized per unique locale

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `attendeesListPromises` maps over `bookingAttendees.attendees` and does `translate: await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")` for each attendee. If many attendees share the same locale (e.g., most are "en"), this results in redundant translation fetches that could be cached/memoized per unique locale for efficiency. This is a performance concern introduced by the new handler, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic inverted: `&&` requires BOTH admin AND owner instead of either, so team admins get FORBIDDEN on bookings they should manage (addGuests.handler.ts ~48)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`: `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. That requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the permission check, which contradicts the variable name and the finding’s claim. As written, a team admin who is not also an owner will fail `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` and get `FORBIDDEN`, matching the reported issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `teamId ?? 0` for non-team bookings makes both isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner checks fail, relying incidentally on isOrganizer to cover it

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` is only used to compute `isTeamAdminOrOwner`. For non-team bookings (no teamId), it correctly makes both `isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner` return false, and access is then governed by the explicit `isOrganizer` / `isAttendee` checks. Nothing in the diff shows this causing incorrect authorization for non-team bookings; it’s expected that team-role checks don’t apply when there is no team.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the organizer's, so attendee-triggered addGuests fails silently or updates the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly allows an attendee to trigger the action (`isAttendee` check, then not forbidden). But the calendar update is executed using the *caller’s* credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, followed by `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. If the caller is an attendee (not the organizer), this will use the attendee’s integrations rather than the booking organizer’s, which can lead to updating the wrong calendar or failing to update the organizer’s calendar when the attendee has no relevant credentials. This is a behavior bug introduced/exposed by allowing attendee-triggered addGuests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema does not enforce guest email uniqueness; duplicate emails pass validation and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows (addGuests.schema.ts:5)

adjudication.rationale: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts only validates that each entry is an email (z.array(z.string().email())) and does not enforce uniqueness. In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array itself. As a result, an input like `["a@example.com", "a@example.com"]` will pass schema validation and both entries will remain in `uniqueGuests`, leading `createMany` to attempt inserting duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but guest is compared raw, so 'Guest@spam.com' bypasses the blacklist
matched_golden_ids: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: the blacklist entries are lowercased but the input guest email is compared without lowercasing, making the includes check case-sensitive and allowing uppercase variants to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee dedupe `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, allowing an already-attending guest to be re-added

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing attendees are filtered with a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., to lowercase), the same email with different casing ("User@x.com" vs "user@x.com") would bypass the dedupe and be added again.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client schema doesn't trim emails, causing inconsistent email validation behavior between UI and API (zod .email() trimming varies by version)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both the client-side validation in `AddGuestsDialog` (`z.array(z.string().email())` + uniqueness refine) and the API input schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` (`z.array(z.string().email())`) using the same Zod `.email()` without any `.trim()`. The PR does not show different Zod versions or any UI/API divergence in trimming behavior, so the claimed inconsistency between UI and API cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Organizer email subject uses calEvent.attendees[0].name instead of team?.name || organizer.name, naming the wrong party and drifting from all other organizer email templates (organizer-add-guests-email.ts:26)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the subject uses `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`, which is plausibly the intended “with {{name}}” value for organizer-facing emails (i.e., the attendee they’re meeting with). The diff does not show any other organizer templates to prove it “drifts from all other organizer email templates,” and the attendee-facing template in this same diff (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`) intentionally uses `team?.name || organizer.name`, so the finding’s proposed change would invert that pattern rather than clearly fix a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Subject template accesses attendees[0].name which throws if the attendees array is empty

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email subject interpolates `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. If `this.calEvent.attendees` is an empty array, this will throw at runtime when building the nodemailer payload. The diff does not guarantee `attendees` is non-empty (it is sourced from DB via `bookingAttendees.attendees` in `addGuests.handler.ts`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws a raw Prisma P2025 surfaced as opaque 500 instead of a typed TRPCError when booking.userId is null

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The code itself suggests `booking.userId` may be falsy/nullable (it falls back to `0`, and `isOrganizer` compares `booking.userId` without assuming it exists). If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this will query `id=0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma not-found error (P2025). There is no surrounding handling to convert that into a `TRPCError`, so it will surface as an internal/opaque server error instead of a typed TRPC error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No seat-capacity validation: seatsPerTimeSlot is read but current attendee count is never checked against capacity before createMany, allowing guests beyond capacity for seated event types

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are appended via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` with no check against any capacity/seat limit. The handler does read `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` when constructing the `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = ...`), but never validates current attendee count + `uniqueGuests.length` against that value before inserting. Whether this is a product-level defect depends on how `seatsPerTimeSlot` is intended to constrain attendees vs. bookings, which is not shown in the diff, but the missing guard is a concrete, diff-grounded gap for seated event types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler returns ad-hoc non-localized raw string { message: "Guests added" } instead of structured data, making untranslated server text part of the public mutation contract

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation ends with `return { message: "Guests added" };`, which is an ad-hoc, non-localized string exposed as part of the mutation response type/contract. The UI shown in the diff does not use this returned `message` (it shows `t("guests_added")` on success), so it’s not a functional defect, but it is a concrete API/design issue introduced by this change: server-returned text is not structured/i18n-friendly and could leak untranslated strings to any consumer that does display it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Authorization logic uses && instead of || in addGuests.handler.ts:55-58, so team admins must also be team owners to pass, causing FORBIDDEN errors for legitimate admins

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and the subsequent authorization gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, this will wrongly block legitimate team admins who are not owners, producing `FORBIDDEN` errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Server accepts duplicate guests within a single request in addGuests.handler.ts:66-72; dedupe only checks existing attendees, allowing direct tRPC calls to create duplicate attendee rows
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: the server-side filtering/deduplication only removes emails already present (or otherwise excluded) but does not deduplicate repeated emails within the incoming request, so createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows when the client submits duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Blacklist check is case-inconsistent (addGuests.handler.ts:60-72); guest emails are compared raw against lowercased blacklist entries, allowing bypass via different casing

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the check uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where `guest` is the raw input string (not lowercased). This makes the blacklist comparison case-sensitive and allows bypass by changing the casing of the guest email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Calendar update failure at addGuests.handler.ts:160-161 is outside try/catch and runs after the Prisma write, leaving DB mutated with no rollback and no emails sent; retry dead-ends on uniqueness check

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the Prisma `booking.update({... attendees.createMany ...})` persists new attendees before the external side-effect `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is executed, and that calendar update is not wrapped in a try/catch or transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the handler fails after the DB mutation. A retry with the same emails will hit `uniqueGuests.length === 0` because `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees`, causing a `BAD_REQUEST` and preventing recovery while also skipping the email notifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Email send errors silently swallowed in addGuests.handler.ts:163-167; error object discarded, wrong console.log used, and user gets success toast even if zero emails delivered

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in a `try/catch` that logs only a fixed string (`console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")`) and discards the caught `err`, then the handler still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" }`). This means the UI success path (toast in `AddGuestsDialog` on mutation success) will occur even if `sendAddGuestsEmails` fails, and failures are poorly observable due to the non-informative log. However, this is not a strictly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone because continuing despite email failures may be an intentional design choice to not block guest addition on notification issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: No cap on number of guests per request (addGuests.schema.ts:3-5); array has no max(), enabling mass attendee creation and email fan-out as a spam/DoS vector

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new authed mutation `addGuests` whose input schema (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`) defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` or other size limit. The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) then `createMany` attendees from this array and triggers `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which can fan out emails across attendees/team members. With no request-size cap shown in the diff, a large `guests` array could cause mass DB writes and email sends, creating a spam/DoS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Client error toast fallback is dead code (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-46); message is always non-empty so t('unable_to_add_guests') unreachable, and t(err.message) may render raw keys

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` is always a non-empty string due to template-string coercion (even when `err.data?.code` is undefined), so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` will never use the fallback. This can result in user-facing toasts like `undefined: <...>` and `t(err.message)` may display raw/untranslated keys if `err.message` isn’t a valid locale key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: isInvalidEmail flag never cleared on retry (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:55-63); stale warning remains visible even after user fixes emails and the request succeeds

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `safeParse` fails, but it is never reset to `false` when the user corrects the emails and retries `handleAdd()` successfully. The only reset is in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`), not in `handleAdd` or mutation callbacks. This means the red warning can remain visible during a subsequent valid submission (until the dialog closes on success). The finding’s claim that it remains visible even after success is slightly overstated because `onSuccess` closes the dialog, but the core issue (stale flag on retry) is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken authorization logic in addGuests.handler.ts: uses `&&` instead of `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so users must be both admin and owner to pass; team admins or owners alone are denied and the admin/owner branch is effectively dead logic
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same authorization bug: using && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner incorrectly requires both roles, and it should be || so either admin or owner is sufficient.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Effective authorization degrades to 'organizer or any existing attendee', allowing any attendee to add arbitrary guests to a booking and trigger emails/calendar updates (potential unintended privilege escalation)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any existing attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the guard only blocks when *none* of `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isOrganizer`, or `isAttendee` is true (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). This means any attendee can call `viewer.bookings.addGuests` to append new attendees (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`), trigger calendar updates (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`), and send emails (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`), matching the finding's privilege-escalation concern. Additionally, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, likely narrowing admin/owner access unintentionally and further pushing effective auth toward organizer/attendee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale pre-update `booking` object is passed to eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees instead of the updated `bookingAttendees`, so new guests may never be synced to the calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code updates the booking via `prisma.booking.update(...)` into `bookingAttendees` (which includes the newly created attendees), but then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using the original `booking` fetched earlier. This is a real diff-grounded inconsistency: the second argument is stale relative to the DB update. Whether this actually prevents calendar syncing can’t be verified from the diff because `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` isn’t shown and it may rely primarily on `evt.attendees` (which *is* built from `bookingAttendees.attendees`). Still, the mismatch is a legitimate review concern and likely should be corrected/clarified by passing an updated booking object (or ensuring the function doesn’t depend on `booking.attendees`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive duplicate/blacklist filtering: `guest === attendee.email` and blacklistedGuestEmails comparison don't lowercase the guest, so `User@example.com` bypasses the blacklist and creates duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased, but `uniqueGuests` filtering compares `guest` without normalizing case: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and duplicates are checked via `guest === attendee.email`. Since the schema only validates `.email()` (no lowercasing), inputs like `User@example.com` can bypass blacklist entries like `user@example.com` and can also bypass duplicate detection against an existing attendee email with different casing, leading to unintended attendee creation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side zod schema in AddGuestsDialog duplicates ZAddGuestsInputSchema; uniqueness rule exists only on the client, so the server doesn't enforce it — reuse the shared server schema and move uniqueness validation server-side

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated validation: `AddGuestsDialog` defines a client-only `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness, while the server-side `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` does not dedupe duplicates within the submitted `guests` array (it only filters against existing attendees and a blacklist), so duplicate emails in the same request can pass server validation and be written via `createMany`, potentially causing a runtime error or inconsistent behavior. This is a correctness issue exposed by the diff, and the finding’s recommendation (shared schema + server-side uniqueness) is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message reuse: `emails_must_be_unique_valid` is used for the 'all guests already exist' case instead of a proper error message

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, when `uniqueGuests.length === 0` (e.g., all provided emails are already in `booking.attendees` or are blacklisted via `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`), the handler throws `new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. That message key implies invalid/duplicate formatting, but this branch can also represent the distinct case "all guests already exist" (or all are blacklisted), so the finding about error message reuse is accurate. This is a UX/message correctness issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Swallowed error in catch block logs a static string ('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') instead of the actual error, making email failures undebuggable; should log err with bookingId via the repo's logger

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which drops the actual `err` details and any context like `bookingId`. This doesn’t directly break the add-guests flow (it still returns success), but it degrades observability/debuggability of real email failures as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BookingListItem renders the add_members action for every booking without checking booking.status, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/rejected bookings; should gate the action and/or validate status server-side

adjudication.rationale: In `BookingListItem`, the new `add_members` action is appended to the `actions` array unconditionally (no check of any booking status before calling `setIsOpenAddGuestsDialog(true)`). On the backend, `addGuestsHandler` updates `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and sends emails, but it does not validate any booking lifecycle/status field before mutating the booking. If cancelled/rejected bookings exist, this diff enables adding guests (and sending notifications/calendar updates) for them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation error state `isInvalidEmail` is never reset on email edits or dialog reopen, only on cancel, so the error sticks for the dialog's lifetime

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). It is not reset when the user edits emails via `MultiEmail` (only `setMultiEmailValue` is called), nor when the dialog is closed/reopened via `Dialog`’s `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` (no effect on `isInvalidEmail`). Since `<AddGuestsDialog ... />` is always mounted in `BookingListItem` and merely toggled with `isOpenDialog`, the error state can persist across dialog reopen and while editing, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: onError uses `t(err.message)` assuming the message is always a translation key; non-TRPC errors render raw text and `${err.data?.code}` leaks internal error codes into the UI toast

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog` the mutation `onError` builds a toast message as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. This explicitly surfaces TRPC error codes like `BAD_REQUEST`/`FORBIDDEN` to end users and assumes `err.message` is always a translation key (otherwise `t(...)` may show a missing-key/raw string). Also, because a template string is always truthy, `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` effectively never uses the fallback for typical errors, making the UX dependent on internal error formatting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail uses array index as React key in value.map, which can cause stale input state on removal/reordering; prefer a stable id per row

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list rendering uses the array index as the React key: `value.map((field, index) => (<li key={index}> ... ))`. Because this component supports removing items (`updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`), using index keys can cause React to reuse the wrong child instance after deletions, which can lead to stale per-row component state/focus (especially if `EmailField` maintains internal state). This is a concrete, diff-grounded issue, but not a guaranteed defect given the inputs are controlled by `value`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Authorization check uses `&&` instead of `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so team admins (non-owners) are wrongly forbidden at addGuests.handler.ts:60-66

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which only returns true if the user is both a team admin and a team owner. The variable name and typical permission semantics imply it should allow either role. As written, a team admin who is not an owner will fail the authorization gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` and be incorrectly forbidden.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Any booking attendee can add an unbounded list of guests with no cap or per-booking status check, enabling email bombing via ICS REQUEST emails even on cancelled/rejected bookings

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation allows any attendee (`isAttendee` check in `addGuests.handler.ts`) to add guests, with no server-side cap (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is just `z.array(z.string().email())`) and the UI (`MultiEmail`) can add unlimited fields. The handler also does not check booking status (no cancelled/rejected/ended guard before updating attendees and calling `sendAddGuestsEmails`). `sendAddGuestsEmails` then sends ICS `REQUEST` emails to organizer/team members and attendees, so a malicious attendee can trigger large volumes of email/calendar updates (potentially even on cancelled bookings).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees will no-op or fail when a non-organizer triggers the mutation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the mutation can be triggered by a non-organizer (it allows `isAttendee` as well as organizer/admin). But the calendar update is performed with credentials fetched from the acting user: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` where `user` is `ctx.user`. The organizer is looked up separately (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) but their credentials are never used. If an attendee triggers this, `updateCalendarAttendees` will run under the attendee’s credentials rather than the booking owner’s, which can cause the calendar update to no-op or fail for the organizer/destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Partial failure — DB write (prisma.booking.update creating attendees) is committed before updateCalendarAttendees, which is outside the try/catch; a throw leaves guests persisted, emails unsent, and calendar out of sync with no reconciliation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no surrounding `try/catch` or DB transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the DB write has already committed, while calendar sync and subsequent email sending (which is separately try/catched) won’t complete—leaving the booking attendees list updated but external calendars potentially out of sync with no rollback/reconciliation shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Seated events bypass seat capacity — guests are inserted directly into booking.attendees with no check against seatsPerTimeSlot or the seated-booking seat structure, allowing arbitrary overbooking

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` (new file `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`), guests are added via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` with no conditional logic around `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` or any other capacity/seated-event constraints. Since the calendar event payload explicitly includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees`, this endpoint can increase `booking.attendees` arbitrarily even for seated events, effectively bypassing any seat-capacity enforcement that would normally limit attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Blacklist and attendee dedupe are bypassed by case variation — blacklist emails are lowercased but `guest` is not, and attendee comparison is case-sensitive, allowing blacklisted emails and duplicate attendee rows with duplicate ICS emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklist entries are normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` values are compared without lowercasing (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Likewise, dedupe against existing attendees is case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email`). This allows bypassing both checks by changing email casing (e.g. `Bad@Example.com` vs `bad@example.com`), potentially inserting duplicate attendee rows and admitting blacklisted addresses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: booking.userId can be null (unassigned bookings), causing findFirstOrThrow({id: booking.userId || 0}) to throw a raw Prisma error resulting in a 500 instead of a handled TRPCError

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is ever null/undefined (or otherwise falsy), this will query `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "not found" error that is not converted into a `TRPCError`, likely surfacing as a 500. The diff doesn’t prove `booking.userId` can be null, but the `|| 0` pattern makes this edge case plausible and worth handling explicitly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Client-side AddGuestsDialog — multiEmailValue can be non-empty while containing only empty strings so handleAdd silently no-ops with no feedback, and isInvalidEmail is never reset on subsequent attempts, leaving a stale error banner

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on validation failure but is never cleared on subsequent submissions or when the dialog is reopened; it’s only reset on the Cancel button handler. Since the component stays mounted (rendered from `BookingListItem` regardless of `isOpenDialog`), a prior invalid attempt can leave a stale error banner visible on later opens and even after a successful submit (`onSuccess` resets `multiEmailValue` but does not reset `isInvalidEmail`). The finding’s claim about “non-empty but only empty strings silently no-ops” is inaccurate (empty strings fail the zod `.email()` check and set `isInvalidEmail`), but the stale error state is a real defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Server schema only validates z.array(z.string().email()) without a uniqueness check, so direct API calls can submit duplicate guests, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: The server input schema in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` but does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails; it does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. As a result, direct API calls can pass `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]`, and `attendees.createMany` will attempt to insert duplicate attendee rows / trigger duplicate notification behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Email send errors are swallowed — console.log with no error object and success returned, so nobody learns guests weren't notified

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in a `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block. This swallows the error (no rethrow / TRPCError), logs without including `err`, and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the client will treat the mutation as successful even if guest notification emails failed.
